This period marked a pivotal change in the poultry industry, with the poultry meat-producing industry becoming more important than the egg-laying industry by the mid-20th century.

### References

- [1] Since their domestication, a large number of breeds of chickens have been established, but with the exception of the white Leghorn, most commercial birds are of hybrid origin. In about 1800, chickens began to be kept on a larger scale, and modern high-output poultry farms were present in the United Kingdom from around 1920 and became established in the United States soon after the Second World War. By the mid-20th century, the poultry meat-producing industry was of greater importance than the egg-laying industry. Poultry breeding has produced breeds and strains to fulfil different needs; light-framed, egg-laying birds that can produce 300 eggs a year; fast-growing, fleshy birds destined for consumption at a young age, and utility birds which produce both an acceptable number of eggs and a well-fleshed carcase. Male birds are unwanted in the egg-laying industry and can often be identified as soon as they are hatch for subsequent culling. In meat breeds, these birds are sometimes castrated (often chemically) to prevent aggression. The resulting bird, called a capon, has more tender and flavorful meat, as well.

Q: With what method is royal assent generally granted?
Gold: letters patent
Answer: Royal assent is generally granted less ceremonially by letters patent. This method is commonly used in various countries, including Australia and Canada, where the governor-general signs the bill to give it royal assent. For instance, in Australia, the governor-general may grant royal assent either in person or by written declaration, while in Canada, the governor general may give assent either in person at a ceremony held in the Senate or by a written declaration notifying parliament of his or her agreement to the bill.

### References

- [1] Royal assent is sometimes associated with elaborate ceremonies. In the United Kingdom, for instance, the sovereign may appear personally in the House of Lords or may appoint Lords Commissioners, who announce that royal assent has been granted at a ceremony held at the Palace of Westminster. However, royal assent is usually granted less ceremonially by letters patent. In other nations, such as Australia, the governor-general merely signs the bill. In Canada, the governor general may give assent either in person at a ceremony held in the Senate or by a written declaration notifying parliament of his or her agreement to the bill.
- [2] In Australia, a technical issue arose with the royal assent in both 1976 and 2001. In 1976, a bill originating in the House of Representatives was mistakenly submitted to the Governor-General and assented to. However, it was later discovered that it had not been passed by each house. The error arose because two bills of the same title had originated from the house. The Governor-General revoked the first assent, before assenting to the bill which had actually passed. The same procedure was followed to correct a similar error which arose in 2001.

#26
Q: How can different range of voltages be supplied for AC locomotives?
Gold: multiple taps on the transformer
Answer: Different ranges of voltages can be supplied for AC locomotives through the use of transformers. Transformers are electrical devices that can provide a range of voltages to the AC locomotive, allowing it to handle various supply voltages for cross-border operation. This capability is essential for modern electric locomotives designed to operate efficiently across different railway networks.

For instance, an AC locomotive can be supplied with a range of voltages via a transformer that has multiple taps. These taps allow the locomotive to receive the appropriate voltage level depending on the specific requirements of the railway network it is operating on. This setup eliminates the need for power-wasting resistors that were previously used in DC locomotives for speed control, making AC locomotives more efficient.

### References

- [1] An early advantage of AC is that the power-wasting resistors used in DC locomotives for speed control were not needed in an AC locomotive: multiple taps on the transformer can supply a range of voltages. Separate low-voltage transformer windings supply lighting and the motors driving auxiliary machinery. More recently, the development of very high power semiconductors has caused the classic "universal" AC/DC motor to be largely replaced with the three-phase induction motor fed by a variable frequency drive, a special inverter that varies both frequency and voltage to control motor speed. These drives can run equally well on DC or AC of any frequency, and many modern electric locomotives are designed to handle different supply voltages and frequencies to simplify cross-border operation.

Q: What other forms of writing materials were used during this period?
Gold: copperplate scrolls
Answer: During the period discussed, several writing materials were used, including palm leaves and paper. Palm leaves were commonly used in Southeast Asia for writing, with each section containing only a few lines written longitudinally and bound together with twine. The outer portion of these palm leaf sections was often decorated. Q: How do quarter wave elements act in relation to a series relevant electrical element?
Gold: imitate
Answer: Quarter-wave elements mimic a series-resonant electrical element through the presence of a standing wave. At the resonant frequency, the standing wave results in a current peak and a voltage node (minimum) at the feed. This configuration allows the element to have minimum reactance, thereby generating the maximum current for the minimum voltage. This ideal situation produces the maximum output for the minimum input, leading to the highest possible efficiency.

### References

At the resonant frequency, the standing wave has a current peak and voltage node (minimum) at the feed. In electrical terms, this means the element has minimum reactance, generating the maximum current for minimum voltage. This is the ideal situation, because it produces the maximum output for the minimum input, producing the highest possible efficiency. Contrary to an ideal (lossless) series-resonant circuit, a finite resistance remains (corresponding to the relatively small voltage at the feed-point) due to the antenna's radiation resistance as well as any actual electrical losses.

Q: What type of Latin was likely spoken in Rome?
Gold: Vulgar Latin
Answer: The native language of the Romans was Vulgar Latin, which significantly differed from the highly stylised and polished Classical Latin. Vulgar Latin was the actual spoken language of the Romans, used in everyday life, while Classical Latin was reserved for literary and formal purposes. Over time, Vulgar Latin evolved into the Romance languages, including Italian, which is one of the languages that evolved from Vulgar Latin.

### References

- [1] The native language of the Romans was Latin. Although surviving Latin literature consists almost entirely of Classical Latin, an artificial and highly stylised and polished literary language from the 1st century BC, the actual spoken language was Vulgar Latin, which significantly differed from Classical Latin in grammar, vocabulary, and eventually pronunciation. Rome's expansion spread Latin throughout Europe, and over time Vulgar Latin evolved and dialectised in different locations, gradually shifting into a number of distinct Romance languages. Many of these languages, including French, Italian, Portuguese, Romanian and Spanish, flourished, the differences between them growing greater over time. Although English is Germanic rather than Roman in origin, English borrows heavily from Latin and Latin-derived words.

It does not harmonize with this or that ensemble; it harmonizes with things in general, with the universe: it is an organism...". #102
Q: What are attacks designed to make a machine or network unavailable to its intended users?
Gold: Denial of service attacks
Answer: Denial of service attacks are designed to make a machine or network resource unavailable to its intended users. These attacks can target individual victims, such as locking their accounts by entering wrong passwords repeatedly, or they can overload the capabilities of a machine or network, blocking all users at once. Such attacks can originate from a single IP address or, more commonly, from a large number of points, making them much harder to defend against. For instance, a botnet can be used to launch a distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack, where innocent systems are fooled into sending traffic to the victim. Additionally, techniques like reflection and amplification attacks can also be employed, where innocent systems are tricked into sending traffic to the victim, thereby amplifying the attack's impact.

### References

- [1] Denial of service attacks are designed to make a machine or network resource unavailable to its intended users. Attackers can deny service to individual victims, such as by deliberately entering a wrong password enough consecutive times to cause the victim account to be locked, or they may overload the capabilities of a machine or network and block all users at once. While a network attack from a single IP address can be blocked by adding a new firewall rule, many forms of Distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks are possible, where the attack comes from a large number of points – and defending is much more difficult. Such attacks can originate from the zombie computers of a botnet, but a range of other techniques are possible including reflection and amplification attacks, where innocent systems are fooled into sending traffic to the victim.

### References

- [1] IBM started working on a prototype system loosely based on Codd's concepts as System R in the early 1970s. Subsequent multi-user versions were tested by customers in 1978 and 1979, by which time a standardized query language – SQL[citation needed] – had been added. Codd's ideas were establishing themselves as both workable and superior to CODASYL, pushing IBM to develop a true production version of System R, known as SQL/DS, and, later, Database 2 (DB2).

#123
Q: In which format does crosstalk generally not occur?
Gold: CAV
Answer: Crosstalk typically does not occur in digital communication systems, such as those used in multipoint conferencing, where data is transmitted in the form of digital streams. A digital stream, as defined, is a sequence of 1s and 0s that represents audio and video data after compression. In digital systems, each bit of data is transmitted independently, reducing the likelihood of interference or crosstalk compared to analog systems.

In a decentralized multipoint conferencing setup, audio and video data are transmitted directly between stations without the need for a central manager. This direct transmission minimizes the risk of crosstalk, as each station handles its own data independently. The advantages of this technique include higher quality video and audio, as the data does not have to be relayed through a central point, and the ability to make ad-hoc multipoint calls without concern for the availability or control of an MCU (Multipoint Control Unit).

### References

- [1] Some systems are capable of multipoint conferencing with no MCU, stand-alone, embedded or otherwise. These use a standards-based H.323 technique known as "decentralized multipoint", where each station in a multipoint call exchanges video and audio directly with the other stations with no central "manager" or other bottleneck.
- [2] The core technology used in a videoconferencing system is digital compression of audio and video streams in real time. The hardware or software that performs compression is called a codec (coder/decoder). Compression rates of up to 1:500 can be achieved. The resulting digital stream of 1s and 0s is subdivided into labeled packets, which are then transmitted through a digital network of some kind (usually ISDN or IP).

He wrote that children can learn better if taught in classes instead of individual tuition from private tutors, and he gave a number of reasons for why this is the case, citing the value of competition and emulation among pupils, as well as the usefulness of group discussions and debates. In Roman religion, for instance, the principle of "do ut des" (I give that you might give) guided many religious practices, including sacrifices. This principle suggests that sacrifices were not just about offering something to the gods but also about establishing a reciprocal relationship where both parties benefit.

For example, in Roman religious practices, the correct performance of rituals and sacrifices was essential for maintaining social order and ensuring the favor of the gods. The household shrine, neighborhood shrines, and sacred places like springs and groves were integral to daily religious life. Sacrifices often involved not just the main offering but also additional items to enhance the ritual's effectiveness and to show respect and gratitude.

### References

- [1] Roman religion was thus practical and contractual, based on the principle of do ut des, "I give that you might give." Religion depended on knowledge and the correct practice of prayer, ritual, and sacrifice, not on faith or dogma, although Latin literature preserves learned speculation on the nature of the divine and its relation to human affairs. Even the most skeptical among Rome's intellectual elite such as Cicero, who was an augur, saw religion as a source of social order. For ordinary Romans, religion was a part of daily life. Each home had a household shrine at which prayers and libations to the family's domestic deities were offered. Neighborhood shrines and sacred places such as springs and groves dotted the city. The Roman calendar was structured around religious observances. Women, slaves, and children all participated in a range of religious activities. Some public rituals could be conducted only by women, and women formed what is perhaps Rome's most famous priesthood, the state-supported Vestals, who tended Rome's sacred hearth for centuries, until disbanded under Christian domination.

According to the information provided, birds use their plumage to assess social dominance, display breeding conditions, and communicate aggression or submission. These visual cues can help distinguish between different species and individuals within a species.

### References

- [1] Birds sometimes use plumage to assess and assert social dominance, to display breeding condition in sexually selected species, or to make threatening displays, as in the sunbittern's mimicry of a large predator to ward off hawks and protect young chicks. Variation in plumage also allows for the identification of birds, particularly between species. Visual communication among birds may also involve ritualised displays, which have developed from non-signalling actions such as preening, the adjustments of feather position, pecking, or other behaviour. These displays may signal aggression or submission or may contribute to the formation of pair-bonds. The most elaborate displays occur during courtship, where "dances" are often formed from complex combinations of many possible component movements; males' breeding success may depend on the quality of such displays.

### References

Higher levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere are thought to have caused the world temperature gradient from north to south to become almost flat: temperatures were about the same across the planet. Average temperatures were also higher than today by about 10°C. In fact, by the middle Cretaceous, equatorial ocean waters (perhaps as warm as 20 °C in the deep ocean) may have been too warm for sea life, and land areas near the equator may have been deserts despite their proximity to water. The circulation of oxygen to the deep ocean may also have been disrupted.

#162
Q: What did a criminal infringer do to be prosecuted?
Gold: for the purpose of commercial advantage or private financial gain
Answer: To be prosecuted for criminal copyright infringement, an individual must engage in actions that violate the copyright law with the intent to gain commercial or financial advantage. Specifically, the infringer must have acted "for the purpose of commercial advantage or private financial gain" and must have possessed the necessary mens rea, or criminal intent.

The prosecution must first demonstrate that the infringer had ownership of a valid copyright and violated one or more of the copyright holder's exclusive rights. Additionally, the government must prove that the infringement was willful, meaning the infringer acted intentionally and with the knowledge that their actions were in violation of the copyright law.

For misdemeanor infringement, the threshold is particularly low, involving a very small number of copies and a minimal value of the infringed works. However, the key elements remain the same: the infringement must be willful and for profit, and the infringer must have the requisite mens rea.

### References

- [1] The first criminal provision in U.S. copyright law was added in 1897, which established a misdemeanor penalty for "unlawful performances and representations of copyrighted dramatic and musical compositions" if the violation had been "willful and for profit." Criminal copyright infringement requires that the infringer acted "for the purpose of commercial advantage or private financial gain." 17 U.S.C. § 506. To establish criminal liability, the prosecutor must first show the basic elements of copyright infringement: ownership of a valid copyright, and the violation of one or more of the copyright holder's exclusive rights. The government must then establish that defendant willfully infringed or, in other words, possessed the necessary mens rea. Misdemeanor infringement has a very low threshold in terms of number of copies and the value of the infringed works.

#164
Q: How does the halogen bulb decrease darkening over time?
Gold: by redepositing tungsten from the inside of the bulb back onto the filament
Answer: The halogen bulb reduces darkening over time through a process known as the halogen cycle. Unlike standard gas-filled lamps, which use an inert gas, halogen lamps are filled with a halogen gas at low pressure. This setup helps to reduce the uneven evaporation of the filament and prevents the darkening of the envelope. 

In the halogen cycle, tungsten atoms from the filament evaporate and deposit on the inner surface of the glass bulb. Instead of being lost, these tungsten atoms are redeposited back onto the filament, maintaining its integrity and preventing darkening. This process allows the filament to operate at a higher temperature than a standard gas-filled lamp of similar power without losing operating life. As a result, the halogen lamp can achieve longer bulb life and reduced darkening compared to traditional incandescent bulbs.

### References

- [1] The halogen lamp reduces uneven evaporation of the filament and eliminates darkening of the envelope by filling the lamp with a halogen gas at low pressure, rather than an inert gas. The halogen cycle increases the lifetime of the bulb and prevents its darkening by redepositing tungsten from the inside of the bulb back onto the filament. The halogen lamp can operate its filament at a higher temperature than a standard gas filled lamp of similar power without loss of operating life. Such bulbs are much smaller than normal incandescent bulbs, and are widely used where intense illumination is needed in a limited space. Fiber-optic lamps for optical microscopy is one typical application.

The reproductive system also matures, preparing the body for sexual activity and eventual fertility.

### References

This is triggered by the pituitary gland, which secretes a surge of hormonal agents into the blood stream, initiating a chain reaction to occur. The male and female gonads are subsequently activated, which puts them into a state of rapid growth and development; the triggered gonads now commence the mass production of the necessary chemicals. The testes primarily release testosterone, and the ovaries predominantly dispense estrogen. The production of these hormones increases gradually until sexual maturation is met. Neither 胡 exists as an independent morpheme except as a poetic abbreviation of the disyllabic word.

### References

In modern Chinese 10% of morphemes only occur as part of a given compound. However, a few morphemes are disyllabic, some of them dating back to Classical Chinese. Excluding foreign loan words, these are typically words for plants and small animals. They are usually written with a pair of phono-semantic compound characters sharing a common radical. Examples are 蝴蝶 húdié "butterfly" and 珊瑚 shānhú "coral". Note that the 蝴 hú of húdié and the 瑚 hú of shānhú have the same phonetic, 胡, but different radicals (\"insect\" and \"jade\", respectively). Neither exists as an independent morpheme except as a poetic abbreviation of the disyllabic word.

Q: A definition of literature that incorporates style and the poetic nature of prose is what?
Gold: formalist
Answer: The formalist definition of literature emphasizes the poetic effects and distinguishes it from ordinary speech or other kinds of writing. According to this definition, literature is characterized by its "literariness" or "poeticity," which are key features that set it apart from everyday language and other forms of writing. This perspective foregrounds the stylistic and aesthetic qualities inherent in literary works, making it a useful framework for understanding the use of the term "literature" in contexts such as scientific literature, where specific language standards are required.

### References

- [1] The formalist definition is that the history of "literature" foregrounds poetic effects; it is the "literariness" or "poeticity" of literature that distinguishes it from ordinary speech or other kinds of writing (e.g., journalism). Jim Meyer considers this a useful characteristic in explaining the use of the term to mean published material in a particular field (e.g., "scientific literature"), as such writing must use language according to particular standards. The problem with the formalist definition is that in order to say that literature deviates from ordinary uses of language, those uses must first be identified; this is difficult because "ordinary language" is an unstable category, differing according to social categories and across history.

Q: What is von Neumann algebra?
Gold: algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space that is closed in the weak operator topology and contains the identity operator
Answer: A von Neumann algebra is a specific type of \(*\)-algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space that is closed in the weak operator topology and contains the identity operator. This algebraic structure was introduced by John von Neumann, who also studied rings of operators, which inspired the development of continuous geometry.

### References

- [1] Von Neumann introduced the study of rings of operators, through the von Neumann algebras. A von Neumann algebra is a \(*\)-algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space that is closed in the weak operator topology and contains the identity operator. The von Neumann bicommutant theorem shows that the analytic definition is equivalent to a purely algebraic definition as an algebra of symmetries. The direct integral was introduced in 1949 by John von Neumann. One of von Neumann's analyses was to reduce the classification of von Neumann algebras on separable Hilbert spaces to the classification of factors.
- [2] Von Neumann founded the field of continuous geometry. It followed his path-breaking work on rings of operators. In mathematics, continuous geometry is an analogue of complex projective geometry, where instead of the dimension of a subspace being in a discrete set 0, 1, ..., n, it can be an element of the unit interval [0,1]. Von Neumann was motivated by his discovery of von Neumann algebras with a dimension function taking a continuous range of dimensions, and the first example of a continuous geometry other than projective space was the projections of the hyperfinite type II factor.

#243
Q: Are transactions limited?
Gold: Each transaction has well defined boundaries
Answer: Transactions are not inherently limited in their scope or usage. They are defined by the programmer using special transaction commands to encapsulate a series of operations over a database or other system. These commands allow the programmer to specify the boundaries of a transaction, which can include reading, writing, or acquiring locks on database objects. The flexibility of transaction commands means that transactions can be as small or as large as needed, depending on the requirements of the application.

For example, a database transaction might involve a single operation, such as updating a single record, or it could encompass a complex series of operations that need to be treated as a single unit of work. The key aspect is that transactions provide a mechanism for ensuring data integrity and fault tolerance by grouping related operations together and providing a way to manage their execution.

### References

- [1] Database transactions can be used to introduce some level of fault tolerance and data integrity after recovery from a crash. A database transaction is a unit of work, typically encapsulating a number of operations over a database (e.g., reading a database object, writing, acquiring lock, etc.), an abstraction supported in database and also other systems. Each transaction has well defined boundaries in terms of which program/code executions are included in that transaction (determined by the transaction's programmer via special transaction commands).

#256
Q: What is long-distance running as a food hunting-gathering technique?
Gold: persistence hunting
Answer: Long-distance running, particularly in the form of persistence hunting, is a food-hunting technique that involves chasing prey until it becomes exhausted and can be caught. This method is still practiced by some modern hunter-gatherer groups and is proposed by the Endurance Running Hypothesis as a key evolutionary force in human development. According to this hypothesis, the ability to run long distances may have provided early humans with a unique hunting strategy, allowing them to pursue and catch prey that other predators could not.

The Endurance Running Hypothesis suggests that persistence hunting was a significant subsistence strategy that could have driven the evolution of certain human characteristics, such as the development of a larger body size, increased sweating capacity, and a more efficient cardiovascular system. This hypothesis does not necessarily contradict the Scavenging Hypothesis, which proposes that early humans obtained food by scavenging. Both subsistence strategies could have coexisted and influenced human evolution.

### References

- [1] According to the endurance running hypothesis, long-distance running as in persistence hunting, a method still practiced by some hunter-gatherer groups in modern times, was likely the driving evolutionary force leading to the evolution of certain human characteristics. This hypothesis does not necessarily contradict the scavenging hypothesis: both subsistence strategies could have been in use – sequentially, alternating or even simultaneously.

#267
Q: In what year did Mahbub ul Haq devise and launch the HDI?
Gold: 1990
Answer: Mahbub ul Haq devised and launched the Human Development Index (HDI) in 1990. This was part of his initiative to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies. The HDI was developed for use in the Human Development Reports, which were annual publications by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) that Haq had also devised and launched.

### References

- [1] The origins of the HDI are found in the annual Development Reports of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). These were devised and launched by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq in 1990 and had the explicit purpose "to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies". To produce the Human Development Reports, Mahbub ul Haq formed a group of development economists including Paul Streeten, Frances Stewart, Gustav Ranis, Keith Griffin, Sudhir Anand, and Meghnad Desai. Working alongside Nobel laureate Amartya Sen, they worked on capabilities and functions that provided the underlying conceptual framework. Haq was sure that a simple composite measure of human development was needed in order to convince the public, academics, and politicians that they can and should evaluate development not only by economic advances but also improvements in human well-being. Sen initially opposed this idea, but he soon went on to help Haq develop the Index. Sen was worried that it was going to be difficult to capture the full complexity of human capabilities in a single index, but Haq persuaded him that only a single number would shift the immediate attention of politicians from economic to human well-being.

#274
Q: What are are side-effects of introduction and invasion?
Gold: Hybridization and introgression
Answer: The side-effects of introduction and invasion include several phenomena that can have significant impacts on local ecosystems and species. These include:

1. **Uncontrolled Hybridization**: This is a form of genetic pollution where hybridization occurs without control, leading to the mixing of genetic material between introduced and native species. This can result in the loss of genetic diversity in the native species and potentially threaten their survival.

2. **Introgression**: This is another side-effect of introduction and invasion, contributing to genetic pollution. Introgression involves the transfer of genetic material from one species to another through hybridization, which can alter the genetic makeup of the native species.

3. **Genetic Swamping**: This is a specific form of genetic pollution that leads to the replacement of local genomes. It occurs when an introduced species has a numerical and/or fitness advantage, leading to the replacement of the local species' genetic material.

4. **Hybridization**: Hybridization is the process of interbreeding between two different species, which can lead to the creation of hybrid offspring. This can have various ecological impacts, including the potential for the hybrid species to outcompete the native species.

### References

- [1] Endemic species can be threatened with extinction through the process of genetic pollution, i.e. uncontrolled hybridization, introgression and genetic swamping.

#295
Q: What did Renaissance painters call the pigment made from cochineal?
Gold: carmine
Answer: During the Renaissance, the pigment made from cochineal was referred to as carmine. This pigment was introduced as a third pigment by early Renaissance painters, alongside traditional lake pigments such as kermes lake and madder lake. Carmine, produced by the cochineal insect, was valued for its fine crimson color, though it required careful handling to prevent color changes.

### References

- [1] The painters of the early Renaissance used two traditional lake pigments, made from mixing dye with either chalk or alum, kermes lake, made from kermes insects, and madder lake, made from the rubia tinctorum plant. With the arrival of cochineal, they had a third, carmine, which made a very fine crimson, though it had a tendency to change color if not used carefully. It was used by almost all the great painters of the 15th and 16th centuries, including Rembrandt, Vermeer, Rubens, Anthony van Dyck, Diego Velázquez and Tintoretto. Later it was used by Thomas Gainsborough, Seurat and J.M.W. Turner.

#298
Q: There is a relationship between the size of the antenna and the size of the wavelength with what antenna type?
Gold: Highly directional
Answer: The relationship between the size of the antenna and the size of the wavelength is particularly relevant for resonant antennas. Resonant antennas, which are typically linear conductors or pairs of such elements, each about a quarter of the wavelength in length (an odd multiple of quarter wavelengths), are designed to resonate at a specific frequency. This means their physical size is closely tied to the wavelength of the radio waves they are intended to transmit or receive. For instance, at lower frequencies (longer wavelengths), resonant antennas need to be significantly larger than the wavelength to function effectively. Conversely, at higher frequencies (UHF, microwaves), the trade-off between performance and physical size is less critical, allowing for smaller antenna designs.

### References

- [1] An antenna transmits and receives radio waves with a particular polarization which can be reoriented by tilting the axis of the antenna in many (but not all) cases. The physical size of an antenna is often a practical issue, particularly at lower frequencies (longer wavelengths). Highly directional antennas need to be significantly larger than the wavelength. Resonant antennas usually use a linear conductor (or element), or pair of such elements, each of which is about a quarter of the wavelength in length (an odd multiple of quarter wavelengths will also be resonant). Antennas that are required to be small compared to the wavelength sacrifice efficiency and cannot be very directional. Fortunately at higher frequencies (UHF, microwaves) trading off performance to obtain a smaller physical size is usually not required.

#305
Q: Low-bandwidth devices are supported with what?
Gold: a special PID value, PRE
Answer: Low-bandwidth devices are supported with a special PID value, PRE. This marks the beginning of a low-bandwidth packet and is used by hubs that normally do not send full-bandwidth packets to low-bandwidth devices. The PRE packet is followed by a brief pause, during which hubs enable their low-bandwidth outputs, already idling in the J state. Then a low-bandwidth packet follows, beginning with a sync sequence and PID byte, and ending with a brief period of SE0.

### References

- [1] Low-bandwidth devices are supported with a special PID value, PRE. This marks the beginning of a low-bandwidth packet, and is used by hubs that normally do not send full-bandwidth packets to low-bandwidth devices. Since all PID bytes include four 0 bits, they leave the bus in the full-bandwidth K state, which is the same as the low-bandwidth J state. It is followed by a brief pause, during which hubs enable their low-bandwidth outputs, already idling in the J state. Then a low-bandwidth packet follows, beginning with a sync sequence and PID byte, and ending with a brief period of SE0. Full-bandwidth devices other than hubs can simply ignore the PRE packet and its low-bandwidth contents, until the final SE0 indicates that a new packet follows.

### References

- [1] In 1906, precipitation hardening alloys were discovered by Alfred Wilm. Precipitation hardening alloys, such as certain alloys of aluminium, copper, and magnesium, are heat-treatable alloys that soften when quenched (cooled quickly), and then harden over time. Although an explanation for the phenomenon was not provided until 1919, duralumin was one of the first "age hardening" alloys to be used, and was soon followed by many others. Because they often exhibit a combination of high strength and low weight, these alloys became widely used in many forms of industry, including the construction of modern aircraft.

Q: The suprachiasmatic nucleus is a small part of what part of the brain?

It regulates circadian rhythms, which are 24-hour cycles of physiological processes driven by rhythmic changes in the expression of clock genes.

### References

- [1] A key component of the arousal system is the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a tiny part of the hypothalamus located directly above the point at which the optic nerves from the two eyes cross. The SCN contains the body's central biological clock. Neurons there show activity levels that rise and fall with a period of about 24 hours, circadian rhythms: these activity fluctuations are driven by rhythmic changes in expression of a set of "clock genes". The SCN continues to keep time even if it is excised from the brain and placed in a dish of warm nutrient solution, but it ordinarily receives input from the optic nerves, through the retinohypothalamic tract (RHT), that allows daily light-dark cycles to calibrate the clock.

Q: What was the romance genre of Divan poetry known as?
Gold: mesnevî

This form of narrative poetry is significant within the tradition of Ottoman Divan poetry, alongside other common genres such as gazels and kasîdes. Examples of mesnevîs include "Leyli and Majnun" by Fuzûlî and "Hüsn ü Aşk" by Şeyh Gâlib.

### References

- [1] Ottoman Divan poetry was a highly ritualized and symbolic art form. From the Persian poetry that largely inspired it, it inherited a wealth of symbols whose meanings and interrelationships—both of similitude (مراعات نظير mura'ât-i nazîr / تناسب tenâsüb) and opposition (تضاد tezâd) were more or less prescribed. Divan poetry was composed through the constant juxtaposition of many such images within a strict metrical framework, thus allowing numerous potential meanings to emerge. The vast majority of Divan poetry was lyric in nature: either gazels (which make up the greatest part of the repertoire of the tradition), or kasîdes. There were, however, other common genres, most particularly the mesnevî, a kind of verse romance and thus a variety of narrative poetry; the two most notable examples of this form are the Leyli and Majnun of Fuzûlî and the Hüsn ü Aşk of Şeyh Gâlib.

Q: What does Hokkien mean?
Gold: Fujian province
Answer: Hokkien, also known as 福建話 (Pe̍h-ōe-jī: hok-kiàn oē; Tâi-lô: Hok-kiàn-uē), is a dialect of Min Nan, primarily used in Southeast Asia. In Chinese linguistics, it is classified under the Quanzhang Division, named after the urban centers Quanzhou and Zhangzhou. The term "Hokkien" itself is not used in Chinese to refer to the dialect; instead, it simply means Fujian province. In Chinese, it is known as 福建话 (Fújiànhuà).

### References

- [1] The term Hokkien (福建; hɔk˥˥kɪɛn˨˩) is itself a term not used in Chinese to refer to the dialect, as it simply means Fujian province. In Chinese linguistics, these dialects are known by their classification under the Quanzhang Division (Chinese: 泉漳片; pinyin: Quánzhāng piàn) of Min Nan, which comes from the first characters of the two main Hokkien urban centers Quanzhou and Zhangzhou. The variety is also known by other terms such as the more general Min Nan (traditional Chinese: 閩南語, 閩南話; simplified Chinese: 闽南语, 闽南话; pinyin: Mǐnnányǔ, Mǐnnánhuà; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Bân-lâm-gí,Bân-lâm-oē) or Southern Min, and Fulaohua (traditional Chinese: 福佬話; simplified Chinese: 福佬话; pinyin: Fúlǎohuà; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Hō-ló-oē). The term Hokkien (Chinese: 福建話; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: hok-kiàn oē;Tâi-lô:Hok-kiàn-uē), on the other hand, is used commonly in South East Asia to refer to Min-nan dialects.

As in all lossy compression, there is a trade-off between video quality, cost of processing the compression and decompression, and system requirements. #372
Q: What is one disadvantage of using the H.323 technique?
Gold: increased network bandwidth
Answer: One disadvantage of using the H.323 technique, specifically when implementing decentralized multipoint conferencing, is the increased network bandwidth required. In a decentralized multipoint setup, every station must transmit directly to every other station, which can lead to higher data usage compared to systems that use a Multi-Point Control Unit (MCU) to manage the traffic.

### References

- [1] Some systems are capable of multipoint conferencing with no MCU, stand-alone, embedded or otherwise. These use a standards-based H.323 technique known as "decentralized multipoint", where each station in a multipoint call exchanges video and audio directly with the other stations with no central "manager" or other bottleneck. The advantages of this technique are that the video and audio will generally be of higher quality because they don't have to be relayed through a central point. Also, users can make ad-hoc multipoint calls without any concern for the availability or control of an MCU. This added convenience and quality comes at the expense of some increased network bandwidth, because every station must transmit to every other station directly.

#393
Q: How is sunlight converted into electricity?
Gold: either directly using photovoltaics (PV), or indirectly using concentrated solar power (CSP)
Answer: Sunlight can be converted into electricity through two primary methods: photovoltaics (PV) and concentrated solar power (CSP).

Photovoltaics (PV) directly converts light into electric current using the photoelectric effect. This method is commonly used in solar panels, where semiconducting materials, such as silicon, absorb sunlight and generate electrical energy (Reference [1]).

Concentrated solar power (CSP) involves using lenses or mirrors and tracking systems to focus a large area of sunlight into a small beam. This concentrated light is then used to heat a fluid, which drives a generator to produce electricity (Reference [2]).

### References

- [1] Solar power is the conversion of sunlight into electricity, either directly using photovoltaics (PV), or indirectly using concentrated solar power (CSP).
- [2] Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) is a method used in solar power to convert sunlight into electricity.

The goal is to provide effective treatment while the precise cause of the infection is being determined.

Q: How were early sacred texts offered?
Gold: orally

The earliest known inscriptions in Sanskrit date to the first century BCE, but the Brahmi script, which was originally used for Prakrit, was employed for writing Sanskrit. This paradoxical situation, where the first evidence of written Sanskrit appears centuries after the Prakrit languages, highlights the transition from oral to written traditions. The sacred texts were set down in writing "reluctantly" (according to one commentator) and at a comparatively late date, indicating that oral transmission was the primary method of maintaining these texts until they were eventually committed to writing.

### References

- [1] The earliest known inscriptions in Sanskrit date to the first century BCE.[citation needed] They are in the Brahmi script, which was originally used for Prakrit, not Sanskrit. It has been described as a paradox that the first evidence of written Sanskrit occurs centuries later than that of the Prakrit languages which are its linguistic descendants. In northern India, there are Brāhmī inscriptions dating from the third century BCE onwards, the oldest appearing on the famous Prakrit pillar inscriptions of king Ashoka. The earliest South Indian inscriptions in Tamil Brahmi, written in early Tamil, belong to the same period. When Sanskrit was written down, it was first used for texts of an administrative, literary or scientific nature. The sacred texts were preserved orally, and were set down in writing "reluctantly" (according to one commentator), and at a comparatively late date.

### References

- [1] Naturally occurring crude asphalt/bitumen impregnated in sedimentary rock is the prime feed stock for petroleum production from "Oil sands", currently under development in Alberta, Canada. Canada has most of the world's supply of natural asphalt/bitumen, covering 140,000 square kilometres (an area larger than England), giving it the second-largest proven oil reserves in the world. The Athabasca oil sands is the largest asphalt/bitumen deposit in Canada and the only one accessible to surface mining, although recent technological breakthroughs have resulted in deeper deposits becoming producible by in situ methods. Because of oil price increases after 2003, producing bitumen became highly profitable, but as a result of the decline after 2014 it became uneconomic to build new plants again. By 2014, Canadian crude asphalt/bitumen production averaged about 2.3 million barrels (370,000 m3) per day and was projected to rise to 4.4 million barrels (700,000 m3) per day by 2020. The total amount of crude asphalt/bitumen in Alberta which could be extracted is estimated to be about 310 billion barrels (50×10^9 m3), which at a rate of 4,400,000 barrels per day (700,000 m3/d) would last about 200 years.

Q: Aristotle thought what would fill any rarity that might give rise to a void?
Gold: denser surrounding material continuum
Answer: Aristotle believed that the denser surrounding material continuum would fill any rarity that might give rise to a void. He used this concept to argue that a natural void could not occur, as the denser material would immediately fill any incipient rarity.

### References

Following Plato, even the abstract concept of a featureless void faced considerable skepticism: it could not be apprehended by the senses, it could not, itself, provide additional explanatory power beyond the physical volume with which it was commensurate and, by definition, it was quite literally nothing at all, which cannot rightly be said to exist. Aristotle believed that no void could occur naturally, because the denser surrounding material continuum would immediately fill any incipient rarity that might give rise to a void.

#430
Q: How is the stimulus interpreted by the mind?
Gold: as a particular emotion
Answer: The interpretation of a stimulus by the mind, according to the James–Lange theory, involves a sequence of physiological responses that are then interpreted as emotions. For example, an emotion-evoking stimulus, such as a snake, triggers a pattern of physiological responses, including increased heart rate and faster breathing. These physiological responses are then interpreted by the mind as a particular emotion, such as fear. This theory suggests that emotions are the result of bodily states, which can be manipulated to induce specific emotional states.

### References

- [1] An example of this theory in action would be as follows: An emotion-evoking stimulus (snake) triggers a pattern of physiological response (increased heart rate, faster breathing, etc.), which is interpreted as a particular emotion (fear). This theory is supported by experiments in which by manipulating the bodily state induces a desired emotional state. Some people may believe that emotions give rise to emotion-specific actions: e.g. "I'm crying because I'm sad," or "I ran away because I was scared." The issue with the James–Lange theory is that of causation (bodily states causing emotions and being a priori), not that of the bodily influences on emotional experience (which can be argued and is still quite prevalent today in biofeedback studies and embodiment theory).

Q: What is the United States Statutes at Large?
Gold: a chronological arrangement of the laws in the exact order that they have been enacted
Answer: The United States Statutes at Large is a collection of bound volumes that compile slip laws at the end of each session of Congress. These volumes present a chronological arrangement of the laws in the exact order that they have been enacted. After the President signs a bill into law, or Congress enacts it over his veto, it is delivered to the Office of the Federal Register (OFR) of the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). The OFR assigns a law number, prepares the slip law, and compiles it into the Statutes at Large at the end of each session. Public laws, but not private laws, are also given legal statutory citation by the OFR.

### References

- [1] The law of the United States comprises many levels of codified and uncodified forms of law, of which the most important is the United States Constitution, the foundation of the federal government of the United States. The Constitution sets out the boundaries of federal law, which consists of acts of Congress, treaties ratified by the Senate, regulations promulgated by the executive branch, and case law originating from the federal judiciary. The United States Code is the official compilation and codification of general and permanent federal statutory law.

Answer: When translating between languages, translators must adjust the syntax characteristics of a text's source language to fit the syntactic requirements of the target language. This process involves reinterpreting the grammatical structure of the source text, which may include shifting from active to passive voice or vice versa. For instance, in "fixed-word-order" languages like English, French, and German, the sentence structure is relatively rigid, whereas "free-word-order" languages such as Greek, Latin, Polish, and Russian allow more flexibility in sentence structure. Translators in these cases must ensure that the translated text adheres to the target language's syntax rules while preserving the original meaning and context.

### References

- [1] In general, translators have sought to preserve the context itself by reproducing the original order of sememes, and hence word order — when necessary, reinterpreting the actual grammatical structure, for example, by shifting from active to passive voice, or vice versa. The grammatical differences between "fixed-word-order" languages (e.g., English, French, German) and "free-word-order" languages (e.g., Greek, Latin, Polish, Russian) have been no impediment in this regard. The particular syntax (sentence-structure) characteristics of a text's source language are adjusted to the syntactic requirements of the target language.

#462
Q: What was introduced in von Neumann algebras?
Gold: study of rings of operators
Answer: Von Neumann algebras, introduced by John von Neumann, are *-algebras of bounded operators on a Hilbert space that are closed in the weak operator topology and contain the identity operator. They are fundamental in the study of operator algebras and have connections to various areas of mathematics and physics.

Key elements introduced in von Neumann algebras include:
- The identity operator, which is a fundamental element in the definition of von Neumann algebras.
- The weak operator topology, which is a topology on the space of bounded operators on a Hilbert space.
- The von Neumann bicommutant theorem, which shows the equivalence of analytic and algebraic definitions.

These concepts were part of von Neumann's broader research on rings of operators, which inspired the development of continuous geometry. His work on von Neumann algebras also led to the introduction of the direct integral, a significant tool in the study of these algebras.

### References

- [1] Von Neumann introduced the study of rings of operators, through the von Neumann algebras.
- [2] Von Neumann founded the field of continuous geometry. It followed his path-breaking work on rings of operators.

Answer: Before the Supreme Court will reverse a decision by a lower court refusing to uphold a constitutional law, the lower court must first enforce an unconstitutional statute. If a lower court enforces an unconstitutional statute, it will be reversed by the Supreme Court. This is based on the principle that no sensible lower court will enforce an unconstitutional statute, and any court that does so will be reversed by the Supreme Court.

### References

- [1] Notably, a statute does not disappear automatically merely because it has been found unconstitutional; it must be deleted by a subsequent statute. Many federal and state statutes have remained on the books for decades after they were ruled to be unconstitutional. However, under the principle of stare decisis, no sensible lower court will enforce an unconstitutional statute, and any court that does so will be reversed by the Supreme Court. Conversely, any court that refuses to enforce a constitutional statute (where such constitutionality has been expressly established in prior cases) will risk reversal by the Supreme Court.

Q: Which CFL games require tie-breaking rounds continue until a winner results?
Gold: playoff or championship
Answer: In the Canadian Football League (CFL), if a game is tied at the end of regulation play, tie-breaking procedures are initiated. These procedures involve a series of rounds where each team gets an equal number of chances to score. Specifically, after the initial round where each team scrimmages the ball at the opponent's 35-yard line, if the game remains tied, the teams continue to alternate possessions from the 35-yard lines. This process continues until one team is leading after both teams have had an equal number of possessions. At that point, the team with the lead is declared the winner.

Q: What year were the earliest known recordings of sound?
Gold: 1857
Answer: The earliest known recordings of sound were made by Léon Scott in 1860 using his phonautograph. These recordings were tracings of sound waves on paper and were not played back as sound until the 2000s when they were digitized and converted into audible sound.

### References

- [1] The phonautograph, patented by Léon Scott in 1857, used a vibrating diaphragm and stylus to graphically record sound waves as tracings on sheets of paper, purely for visual analysis and without any intent of playing them back. In the 2000s, these tracings were first scanned by audio engineers and digitally converted into audible sound. Phonautograms of singing and speech made by Scott in 1860 were played back as sound for the first time in 2008. Along with a tuning fork tone and unintelligible snippets recorded as early as 1857, these are the earliest known recordings of sound.

#530
Q: Coordinative definition has how many major features?
Gold: two
Answer: Coordinative definition has two major features. The first feature involves coordinating units of length with specific physical objects, such as the Standard Metre at the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures or the wavelength of cadmium. The second feature addresses the limitation of directly testing the equality of length for distant objects. Even if two objects appear equal when brought near, we cannot assume they are always equal in length. This necessity leads to the definition of sameness of length by convention.

### References

- [1] Coordinative definition has two major features. The first has to do with coordinating units of length with certain physical objects. This is motivated by the fact that we can never directly apprehend length. Instead we must choose some physical object, say the Standard Metre at the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (International Bureau of Weights and Measures), or the wavelength of cadmium to stand in as our unit of length. The second feature deals with separated objects. Although we can, presumably, directly test the equality of length of two measuring rods when they are next to one another, we can not find out as much for two rods distant from one another. Even supposing that two rods, whenever brought near to one another are seen to be equal in length, we are not justified in stating that they are always equal in length. This impossibility undermines our ability to decide the equality of length of two distant objects. Sameness of length, to the contrary, must be set by definition.

Q: How are Christmas colored light bulbs created?

Additionally, manufacturers may add pigments to the kaolin, a white, chalky clay, which is blown in and electrostatically deposited on the interior of the bulb. This process diffuses the light emitted from the filament, producing a more gentle and evenly distributed light. The colored glass or kaolin-coated bulbs are used to create the vibrant and festive colors seen in Christmas tree lights and other decorative lighting.

### References

- [1] Most light bulbs have either clear or coated glass. The coated glass bulbs have a white powdery substance on the inside called kaolin. Kaolin, or kaolinite, is a white, chalky clay in a very fine powder form, that is blown in and electrostatically deposited on the interior of the bulb. It diffuses the light emitted from the filament, producing a more gentle and evenly distributed light. Manufacturers may add pigments to the kaolin to adjust the characteristics of the final light emitted from the bulb. Kaolin diffused bulbs are used extensively in interior lighting because of their comparatively gentle light. Other kinds of colored bulbs are also made, including the various colors used for "party bulbs", Christmas tree lights and other decorative lighting. These are created by coloring the glass with a dopant; which is often a metal like cobalt (blue) or chromium (green). ### References

- [1] Oklahoma is located in a humid subtropical region. Oklahoma lies in a transition zone between humid continental climate to the north, semi-arid climate to the west, and humid subtropical climate in the central, south and eastern portions of the state. Most of the state lies in an area known as Tornado Alley characterized by frequent interaction between cold, dry air from Canada, warm to hot, dry air from Mexico and the Southwestern U.S., and warm, moist air from the Gulf of Mexico. The interactions between these three contrasting air currents produces severe weather (severe thunderstorms, damaging thunderstorm winds, large hail and tornadoes) with a frequency virtually unseen anywhere else on planet Earth. An average 62 tornadoes strike the state per year—one of the highest rates in the world.

#657
Q: What bacterium is used to produced GM cotton?
Gold: Bacillus thuringiensis
Answer: Genetically modified (GM) cotton, also known as Bt cotton, incorporates the gene from *Bacillus thuringiensis* (Bt) to produce a natural insecticide. This bacterium naturally produces a chemical harmful only to a small fraction of insects, such as the larvae of moths and butterflies, beetles, and flies. By inserting the gene coding for Bt toxin into cotton, the plant can produce this natural insecticide in its tissues, providing protection against pests.

### References

- [1] Genetically modified (GM) cotton was developed to reduce the heavy reliance on pesticides. The bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) naturally produces a chemical harmful only to a small fraction of insects, most notably the larvae of moths and butterflies, beetles, and flies, and harmless to other forms of life. The gene coding for Bt toxin has been inserted into cotton, causing cotton, called Bt cotton, to produce this natural insecticide in its tissues. In many regions, the main pests in commercial cotton are lepidopteran larvae, which are killed by the Bt protein in the transgenic cotton they eat. This eliminates the need to use large amounts of broad-spectrum insecticides to kill lepidopteran pests (some of which have developed pyrethroid resistance). This spares natural insect predators in the farm ecology and further contributes to noninsecticide pest management.

Q: What is the main phytochrome found in seedling grown in light?
Gold: phyB
Answer: The main phytochrome found in seedlings grown in light is PhyB. PhyB is more stable under light conditions compared to other phytochromes like PhyA, PhyC, and PhyD, which are less stable and degrade more readily in light. This stability allows PhyB to play a crucial role in light-dependent processes in seedlings.

### References

- [1] Light is the signal by which plants synchronize their internal clocks to their environment and is sensed by a wide variety of photoreceptors. Red and blue light are absorbed through several phytochromes and cryptochromes. One phytochrome, phyA, is the main phytochrome in seedlings grown in the dark but rapidly degrades in light to produce Cry1. Phytochromes B–E are more stable with phyB, the main phytochrome in seedlings grown in the light. The cryptochrome (cry) gene is also a light-sensitive component of the circadian clock and is thought to be involved both as a photoreceptor and as part of the clock's endogenous pacemaker mechanism. Cryptochromes 1–2 (involved in blue–UVA) help to maintain the period length in the clock through a whole range of light conditions.

### References

- [1] Thirteen thousand species of plants have been identified in the Alpine regions. Alpine plants are grouped by habitat and soil type which can be limestone or non-calcerous. The habitats range from meadows, bogs, woodland (deciduous and coniferous) areas to soilless scree and moraines, and rock faces and ridges. A natural vegetation limit with altitude is given by the presence of the chief deciduous trees—oak, beech, ash and sycamore maple. These do not reach exactly to the same elevation, nor are they often found growing together; but their upper limit corresponds accurately enough to the change from a temperate to a colder climate that is further proved by a change in the presence of wild herbaceous vegetation. This limit usually lies about 1,200 m (3,940 ft) above the sea on the north side of the Alps, but on the southern slopes it often rises to 1,500 m (4,920 ft), sometimes even to 1,700 m (5,580 ft).

Q: Following the Carolingian unification, the term Ashkenazi came to refer to the Jews of what two places?

### References

- [1] Sometime in the early medieval period, the Jews of central and eastern Europe came to be called by this term. In conformity with the custom of designating areas of Jewish settlement with biblical names, Spain was denominated Sefarad (Obadiah 20), France was called Tsarefat (1 Kings 17:9), and Bohemia was called the Land of Canaan. By the high medieval period, Talmudic commentators like Rashi began to use Ashkenaz/Eretz Ashkenaz to designate Germany, earlier known as Loter, where, especially in the Rhineland communities of Speyer, Worms and Mainz, the most important Jewish communities arose. Rashi uses leshon Ashkenaz (Ashkenazi language) to describe German speech, and Byzantium and Syrian Jewish letters referred to the Crusaders as Ashkenazim. Given the close links between the Jewish communities of France and Germany following the Carolingian unification, the term Ashkenazi came to refer to both the Jews of medieval Germany and France.

Immunology rests on an understanding of the properties of these two biological entities and the cellular response to both.

#738
Q: What is database storage?
Gold: physical materialization of a database
Answer: Database storage is the container for the physical materialization of a database. It comprises the internal level in the database architecture and contains all the information needed, such as metadata and internal data structures, to reconstruct the conceptual and external levels from the internal level when required. This storage is managed by the database engine, also known as the "storage engine," which is responsible for putting data into permanent storage.

### References

- [1] Database storage is the container of the physical materialization of a database. It comprises the internal (physical) level in the database architecture. It also contains all the information needed (e.g., metadata, "data about the data," and internal data structures) to reconstruct the conceptual level and external level from the internal level when needed. Putting data into permanent storage is generally the responsibility of the database engine a.k.a. "storage engine." Though typically accessed by a DBMS through the underlying operating system (and often utilizing the operating systems' file systems as intermediates for storage layout), storage properties and configuration setting are extremely important for the efficient operation of the DBMS, and thus are closely maintained by database administrators. A DBMS, while in operation, always has its database residing in several types of storage (e.g., memory and external storage). The database data and the additional needed information, possibly in very large amounts, are coded into bits. Data typically reside in the storage in structures that look completely different from the way the data look in the conceptual and external levels, but in ways that attempt to optimize (the best possible) these levels' reconstruction when needed by users and programs, as well as for computing additional types of needed information from the data (e.g., when querying the database).

Q: How many recordings did Kind Oliver's Creole Jazz band require?
Gold: 13

### References

- [1] The playing time of a phonograph record depended on the turntable speed and the groove spacing. At the beginning of the 20th century, the early discs played for two minutes, the same as early cylinder records. The 12-inch disc, introduced by Victor in 1903, increased the playing time to three and a half minutes. Because a 10-inch 78 rpm record could hold about three minutes of sound per side and the 10-inch size was the standard size for popular music, almost all popular recordings were limited to around three minutes in length. For example, when King Oliver's Creole Jazz Band, including Louis Armstrong on his first recordings, recorded 13 sides at Gennett Records in Richmond, Indiana, in 1923, one side was 2:09 and four sides were 2:52–2:59.

#750
Q: What is a commonly seen example?
Gold: double happiness symbol
Answer: A commonly seen example is the transition from the Julian calendar to the Gregorian calendar. The Gregorian calendar, introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582, replaced the Julian calendar in many countries due to the need for a more accurate calendar system. This transition was necessary because the Julian calendar had accumulated a drift of about 10 days from the solar year, causing discrepancies in the calculation of dates and religious festivals.

For instance, in 1582, when the Gregorian calendar was adopted by Catholic countries, the date of October 4 was followed by October 15, effectively skipping 10 days to correct the calendar drift. This example illustrates how a significant change in calendar systems can impact the way dates are recorded and perceived.

### References

- [1] "Old Style" (OS) and "New Style" (NS) are sometimes added to dates to identify which system is used in the British Empire and other countries that did not immediately change. Because the Calendar Act of 1750 altered the start of the year, and also aligned the British calendar with the Gregorian calendar, there is some confusion as to what these terms mean. They can indicate that the start of the Julian year has been adjusted to start on 1 January (NS) even though contemporary documents use a different start of year (OS); or to indicate that a date conforms to the Julian calendar (OS), formerly in use in many countries, rather than the Gregorian calendar (NS).

#752
Q: How much land did Bronck eventually own?
Gold: 500 acres
Answer: Jonas Bronck eventually accumulated 500 acres (about 2 square km, or 3/4 of a square mile) between the Harlem River and the Aquahung, which became known as Bronck's River, or The Bronx. This land was acquired through leasing from the Dutch West India Company and additional tracts from local tribes.

### References

- [1] Jonas Bronck (c. 1600–43) was a Swedish born emigrant from Komstad, Norra Ljunga parish in Småland, Sweden who arrived in New Netherland during the spring of 1639. He became the first recorded European settler in the area now known as the Bronx. He leased land from the Dutch West India Company on the neck of the mainland immediately north of the Dutch settlement in Harlem (on Manhattan island), and bought additional tracts from the local tribes. He eventually accumulated 500 acres (about 2 square km, or 3/4 of a square mile) between the Harlem River and the Aquahung, which became known as Bronck's River, or The Bronx. Dutch and English settlers referred to the area as Bronck's Land. The American poet William Bronk was a descendant of Pieter Bronck, either Jonas Bronck's son or his younger brother.

#753
Q: At the time change to DST, what will a digital clock read just after 01:59:59.9?
Gold: 03:00:00.0
Answer: Just after 01:59:59.9, a digital clock will jump to 03:00:00.0. This phenomenon occurs because the transition to Daylight Saving Time (DST) in the United States involves a one-hour shift. Specifically, the clock will skip from 01:59:59.9 directly to 03:00:00.0, resulting in a day with 23 hours. This is due to the transition from 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST, as described in the context.

### References

- [1] In the case of the United States where a one-hour shift occurs at 02:00 local time, in spring the clock jumps forward from the last moment of 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST and that day has 23 hours, whereas in autumn the clock jumps backward from the last moment of 01:59 DST to 01:00 standard time, repeating that hour, and that day has 25 hours. A digital display of local time does not read 02:00 exactly at the shift to summer time, but instead jumps from 01:59:59.9 forward to 03:00:00.0.

Q: Prose in the Ottoman empire did not develop to a higher level until which century?
Gold: the 19th century
Answer: Until the 19th century, Ottoman prose did not develop to the extent that contemporary Divan poetry did. This was largely due to the constraints imposed by the rules of sec (سجع, also transliterated as seci), a type of rhymed prose that prescribed a rhyme between each adjective and noun in a string of words. However, despite these limitations, there was still a tradition of prose, though it was primarily non-fictional in nature. Notable examples include Muhayyelât (\"Fancies\") by Giritli Ali Aziz Efendi, a collection of stories of the fantastic written in 1796, and the first novel published in the Ottoman Empire, The Story of Akabi (Turkish: Akabi Hikyayesi), published in 1851.

The central panel of this mosaic floor depicts hunting and fishing scenes, while another panel illustrates the most important cities of the region. The frame of the mosaic is particularly decorative, and it overlays an earlier, damaged mosaic floor from the 6th century.

### References

- [1] The mosaics of the Church of St Stephen in ancient Kastron Mefaa (now Umm ar-Rasas) were made in 785 (discovered after 1986). The perfectly preserved mosaic floor is the largest one in Jordan. On the central panel hunting and fishing scenes are depicted while another panel illustrates the most important cities of the region. The frame of the mosaic is especially decorative. Six mosaic masters signed the work: Staurachios from Esbus, Euremios, Elias, Constantinus, Germanus and Abdela. It overlays another, damaged, mosaic floor of the earlier (587) "Church of Bishop Sergius." Another four churches were excavated nearby with traces of mosaic decoration.

#840
Q: If the plate area and separation distance are altered while keeping the amount of dielectric the same, what effect is had on the maximum energy of the capacitor?
Gold: no change of the maximum amount of energy
Answer: When the plate area and separation distance are altered while maintaining the same dielectric volume, the maximum energy stored in the capacitor remains unchanged. This is because the maximum energy \( E \) that a capacitor can store is primarily determined by the dielectric volume, permittivity, and dielectric strength, as described by the equation:

\[ E = \frac{1}{2} C V^2 \]

where \( C \) is the capacitance and \( V \) is the voltage. The capacitance \( C \) itself is given by:

\[ C = \frac{\epsilon A}{d} \]

Here, \( \epsilon \) is the permittivity of the dielectric, \( A \) is the plate area, and \( d \) is the separation distance between the plates. As long as the dielectric volume remains constant, the product of the plate area and the inverse of the separation distance (which is a form of the capacitance) will adjust to maintain the same energy storage capacity.

### References

- [1] The maximum energy is a function of dielectric volume, permittivity, and dielectric strength. Changing the plate area and the separation between the plates while maintaining the same volume causes no change of the maximum amount of energy that the capacitor can store, so long as the distance between plates remains much smaller than both the length and width of the plates.

#857
Q: What can cause osmotic diarrhea in healthy people?
Gold: too much magnesium or vitamin C or undigested lactose
Answer: Osmotic diarrhea in healthy individuals can be caused by several factors, including the intake of certain substances that draw water into the bowels. For instance, solutions with excessive sugar or salt can cause osmotic diarrhea by drawing water from the body into the bowel. Additionally, high intake of dairy products can lead to osmotic diarrhea in individuals with lactose intolerance, as the undigested lactose can pull in water. Excessive amounts of magnesium or vitamin C can also result in osmotic diarrhea. Sugar alcohols, such as sorbitol, which are often found in sugar-free foods, are difficult for the body to absorb and can cause osmotic diarrhea in large amounts.

### References

- [1] Osmotic diarrhea occurs when too much water is drawn into the bowels. If a person drinks solutions with excessive sugar or excessive salt, these can draw water from the body into the bowel and cause osmotic diarrhea. Osmotic diarrhea can also be the result of maldigestion (e.g., pancreatic disease or Coeliac disease), in which the nutrients are left in the lumen to pull in water. Or it can be caused by osmotic laxatives (which work to alleviate constipation by drawing water into the bowels). In healthy individuals, too much magnesium or vitamin C or undigested lactose can produce osmotic diarrhea and distention of the bowel. A person who has lactose intolerance can have difficulty absorbing lactose after an extraordinarily high intake of dairy products. In persons who have fructose malabsorption, excess fructose intake can also cause diarrhea. High-fructose foods that also have a high glucose content are more absorbable and less likely to cause diarrhea. Sugar alcohols such as sorbitol (often found in sugar-free foods) are difficult for the body to absorb and, in large amounts, may lead to osmotic diarrhea. In most of these cases, osmotic diarrhea stops when offending agent (e.g., milk, sorbitol) is stopped.

#875
Q: The mathematical statement of computers versatility is known as what?
Gold: The Church–Turing thesis
Answer: The mathematical statement of computers' versatility is known as the Church–Turing thesis. This thesis asserts that any function that can be computed by a human using a paper and pencil can also be computed by a Turing machine, which is a theoretical model of a computer. Therefore, any type of computer, whether it is a netbook, supercomputer, or cellular automaton, is capable of performing the same computational tasks, given enough time and storage capacity.

### References

- [1] The ability to store and execute lists of instructions called programs makes computers extremely versatile, distinguishing them from calculators. The Church–Turing thesis is a mathematical statement of this versatility: any computer with a minimum capability (being Turing-complete) is, in principle, capable of performing the same tasks that any other computer can perform. Therefore, any type of computer (netbook, supercomputer, cellular automaton, etc.) is able to perform the same computational tasks, given enough time and storage capacity.

Cephalopods such as the octopus and squid have the largest brains of any invertebrates.

Q: How high of a temperature change can glass-ceramics handle?
Gold: 1000 °C
Answer: Glass-ceramics can handle repeated and quick temperature changes up to 1000 °C. This remarkable property is due to their unique composition and structure, which allows them to sustain such extreme conditions without suffering thermal shock. The balance between the negative thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) of the crystalline ceramic phase and the positive CTE of the glassy phase, achieved at a certain crystallinity level (approximately 70% crystalline), contributes to their excellent mechanical properties and thermal shock resistance.

### References

- [1] The term mainly refers to a mix of lithium and aluminosilicates that yields an array of materials with interesting thermomechanical properties. The most commercially important of these have the distinction of being impervious to thermal shock. Thus, glass-ceramics have become extremely useful for countertop cooking. The negative thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) of the crystalline ceramic phase can be balanced with the positive CTE of the glassy phase. At a certain point (~70% crystalline) the glass-ceramic has a net CTE near zero. This type of glass-ceramic exhibits excellent mechanical properties and can sustain repeated and quick temperature changes up to 1000 °C.

Q: What are the natural theories of law that that the English judges in the eighteenth century used?
Gold: law was believed to have an existence independent of what individual judges said
Answer: During the eighteenth century, English judges subscribed to natural law theories, which posited that law had an existence independent of what individual judges said. According to these theories, judges saw themselves as merely declaring the law that had always theoretically existed, rather than making the law. Consequently, a judge could reject another judge's opinion as an incorrect statement of the law, similar to how scientists might reject each other's conclusions as incorrect statements of scientific laws.

This perspective was prevalent among judges like James Wilson and George Mason, who, during the Philadelphia Convention in 1787, emphasized that laws, even if unjust, could still be legally binding. They argued that judges had the authority to declare unconstitutional laws void but were not to invalidate laws simply because they were unjust or pernicious.

### References

- [1] As federal judge Alex Kozinski has pointed out, binding precedent as we know it today simply did not exist at the time the Constitution was framed. Judicial decisions were not consistently, accurately, and faithfully reported on both sides of the Atlantic (reporters often simply rewrote or failed to publish decisions which they disliked), and the United Kingdom lacked a coherent court hierarchy prior to the end of the 19th century. Furthermore, English judges in the eighteenth century subscribed to now-obsolete natural law theories of law, by which law was believed to have an existence independent of what individual judges said. Judges saw themselves as merely declaring the law which had always theoretically existed, and not as making the law. Therefore, a judge could reject another judge's opinion as simply an incorrect statement of the law, in the way that scientists regularly reject each other's conclusions as incorrect statements of the laws of science.

The first practical implementation of an audio perceptual coder (OCF) in hardware (Krasner's hardware was too cumbersome and slow for practical use), was an implementation of a psychoacoustic transform coder based on Motorola 56000 DSP chips.

#953
Q: What usually changes when a place observes DST?
Gold: The name of local time
Answer: When a place observes Daylight Saving Time (DST), several changes occur, primarily related to the adjustment of local time. Specifically, clocks are moved forward by one hour during the transition to DST. This shift typically results in a day with 23 hours when the transition from 01:59 standard time to 02:00 local time happens, and a day with 25 hours when the transition from 02:00 local time to 03:00 DST occurs. For example, in the United States, the transition from 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST on the last Sunday in March results in a day with 23 hours, while the transition from 03:00 DST to 01:00 standard time on the first Sunday in November results in a day with 25 hours. This adjustment can cause disruptions in software and devices that need to be updated with the correct DST rules, as highlighted by the need to update programmable thermostats or manually adjust clocks.

### References

- [1] "Old Style" (OS) and "New Style" (NS) are sometimes added to dates to identify which system is used in the British Empire and other countries that did not immediately change.
- [2] Damage to a German steel facility occurred during a DST transition in 1993, when a computer timing system linked to a radio time synchronization signal allowed molten steel to cool for one hour less than the required duration, resulting in spattering of molten steel when it was poured.
- [3] In the case of the United States where a one-hour shift occurs at 02:00 local time, in spring the clock jumps forward from the last moment of 01:59 standard time to 03:00 DST and that day has 23 hours, whereas in autumn the clock jumps backward from the last moment of 01:59 DST to 01:00 standard time, repeating that hour, and that day has 25 hours. A digital display of local time does not read 02:00 exactly at the shift to summer time, but instead jumps from 01:59:59.9 forward to 03:00:00.0.
- [4] Consumers must update devices such as programmable thermostats with the correct DST rules, or manually adjust the devices

They also advanced the idea of a transitional stage between the PPNA and PPNB between 8,800 and 8,600 BC at sites like Jerf el Ahmar and Tell Aswad.

Q: What field did Von Neuman establish?
Gold: continuous geometry.
Answer: Von Neumann established the field of game theory as a mathematical discipline. He proved his minimax theorem in 1928, which is foundational in the study of zero-sum games with perfect information. This theorem establishes that in such games, there exists a pair of strategies for both players that allows each to minimize their maximum losses.

### References

- [1] Von Neumann founded the field of game theory as a mathematical discipline. Von Neumann proved his minimax theorem in 1928. This theorem establishes that in zero-sum games with perfect information (i.e. in which players know at each time all moves that have taken place so far), there exists a pair of strategies for both players that allows each to minimize his maximum losses, hence the name minimax. When examining every possible strategy, a player must consider all the possible responses of his adversary. The player then plays out the strategy that will result in the minimization of his maximum loss.
